---
title: "How do Americans View their Leaders?"
---

How do Americans view their leaders, and how does public sentiment toward the White House compare to attitudes toward Congress and political parties? By analyzing monthly Gallup polling data from 1945 to 2026, we can track how public approval, congressional approval, and party favorability interact across various presidential administrations.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 8.2
#| fig-width: 10.5
#| dpi: 300

library(tidyverse)

# Load monthly datasets
monthly_data <- read_csv("data/presidential_approval_by_month.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  arrange(year_month) |>
  mutate(series = "Presidential Approval (1945–2026)", value = approval)

congress_data <- read_csv("data/congressional_approval_by_month.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  arrange(year_month) |>
  mutate(series = "Congressional Approval (1974–2025)", value = approval)

party_data <- read_csv("data/party_favorability_by_month.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  arrange(year_month) |>
  mutate(series = "Party Favorability (1992–2025)", value = favorability)

# Combine into stacked series
combined <- bind_rows(monthly_data, congress_data, party_data) |>
  mutate(series = factor(series, levels = c(
    "Presidential Approval (1945–2026)",
    "Congressional Approval (1974–2025)",
    "Party Favorability (1992–2025)"
  )))

ggplot(combined, aes(x = year_month, y = value)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", color = "#CBD5E1", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_area(aes(fill = series), alpha = 0.14) +
  geom_line(aes(color = series), linewidth = 0.95) +
  facet_wrap(~series, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Presidential Approval (1945–2026)" = "#1D4ED8",
    "Congressional Approval (1974–2025)" = "#7E22CE",
    "Party Favorability (1992–2025)" = "#047857"
  )) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Presidential Approval (1945–2026)" = "#3B82F6",
    "Congressional Approval (1974–2025)" = "#A855F7",
    "Party Favorability (1992–2025)" = "#10B981"
  )) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 105),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 25),
    labels = \(y) paste0(y, "%")
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    limits = c(as.Date("1945-01-01"), as.Date("2026-12-31")),
    date_breaks = "10 years",
    date_labels = "%Y"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Three Eras of American Sentiment (1945–2026)",
    subtitle = "Monthly Gallup ratings for the Presidency, Congress, and Political Parties. Dashed line marks the 50% threshold.",
    caption = "Source: Gallup Historical Trends • Data: 1945–2026",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, color = "#0F172A", margin = margin(b = 4)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10.5, color = "#475569", margin = margin(b = 16)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "#94A3B8", margin = margin(t = 12)),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, color = "#1E293B", hjust = 0, margin = margin(b = 6, t = 8)),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#F1F5F9", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#F8FAFC", linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "#64748B", size = 9),
    panel.spacing = unit(1.4, "lines")
  )
```

### Key Patterns

- **Presidential Approval:** Typically starts highest during an administration's early months, with notable surges during major national crises (such as late 2001) before trending toward polarized ranges.
- **Congressional Approval:** Stays consistently below presidential ratings and regularly sits below 30%, reflecting longstanding public dissatisfaction with the legislative branch regardless of party control.
- **Party Favorability:** Closely tracks broader partisan dynamics, showing increasing polarization and lower favorability over recent decades.
